# What is enterprise content management software (ECM)?

09/23/2026 10:33
\| [Bärbel Heuser-Roth](https://www.doxis.com/en/blog/authorprofile/heuser-roth)

![](https://www.doxis.com/files/content/images/blog/2026/Product%20Blog/ECM%20UK%20%282%29.png)

An FCA-regulated firm gets an audit request for a signed contract from three years ago. Nobody is quite sure whether the master copy sits in the shared drive, the old archive or someone's inbox. That gap between "the information exists somewhere" and "we can produce it in ten minutes" is the problem enterprise content management (ECM) software was built to close.

According to [Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/document-management) (2026), 70% to 90% of enterprise data is unstructured, sitting in documents, emails and files. Picture a large UK organisation with decades of contracts, invoices and case files spread across its ERP, its CRM, a dozen file shares and a legacy archive. Finding one document takes longer than it should.

This guide explains what ECM is, how it works, where it earns its keep across regulated industries, and what changes when you replace an ageing platform like Documentum or FileNet with a modern one.

## Key takeaways

- ECM is enterprise-wide software for capturing, managing, storing and securely delivering business content, connected to the ERP, CRM and Microsoft 365 applications your teams already use
- It solves a specific problem: information scattered across shared drives, inboxes and legacy archives that nobody can search, govern or prove compliant on demand
- UK enterprises across financial services, manufacturing, energy and logistics rely on ECM for jobs like KYC onboarding, claims files and [contract management](https://www.doxis.com/en/solutions/contract-management), all under UK GDPR and FCA retention rules
- Doxis has documented, production-proven migration support for named legacy systems, including Documentum and FileNet, delivered with its migration partner HAVI Solutions
- ECM is now one layer of a broader shift toward Intelligent Content Automation, where ECM, business process management (BPM) and AI-driven document processing run as a single platform

## What is ECM?

Enterprise content management (ECM) is enterprise-wide software that captures, manages, stores, preserves and delivers business content in a secure, audit-ready way. It connects documents and data to the systems that run the business, such as your ERP (SAP, Oracle or Microsoft Dynamics 365), your CRM and Microsoft 365, so information stays findable and governed.

## How does ECM work?

ECM follows the shape of the document lifecycle itself. Everything starts with [document capture](https://www.doxis.com/en/blog/document-capture): a scanned invoice, an emailed contract, a report generated in your ERP. Once captured, it is classified and tagged with metadata. Who sent it? What type of document is it? Which business process does it belong to, and how long must it legally be kept?

From there, the platform manages access and version control. The right people find, edit and share content, and duplicate copies stop drifting out of sync.

[Retention and archiving rules](https://www.doxis.com/en/business-platform/archiving) run in the background. The platform applies the correct retention period to each record automatically, so compliance never depends on someone remembering to delete a file. When an auditor, a customer service agent or a claims handler needs a document, ECM delivers it through a single search across every connected system.

The strongest ECM platforms extend this with AI. [Automatic classification and metadata extraction](https://www.doxis.com/en/blog/document-classification-with-ai) take over most of the manual tagging work. Natural language search lets a compliance officer ask a direct question about a case file and get the answer, with no guessing at folder names.

## Key benefits of ECM for enterprise IT teams

Most large UK organisations already have some form of document storage. What ECM adds is a governed, single source of truth on top of it.

- Fewer information silos: file shares, inboxes and department-level tools consolidate into one platform, so IT maintains and secures one system in place of a patchwork
- Faster response times: customer-facing and case-handling teams pull up the right document in seconds and resolve the case themselves
- Audit-ready compliance: [information governance](https://www.doxis.com/en/business-platform/information-governance) features such as retention rules, access logs and version history live in the platform, so producing evidence for an FCA or UK GDPR audit is a search
- Lower total cost of ownership: retiring redundant archiving, filing and workflow software cuts the number of systems IT has to patch, license and support
- Room to scale: a new department, use case or acquisition extends straight onto the platform you already run

## Common use cases: where ECM earns its keep

The shape of the problem changes by industry. The underlying job stays the same: get the right document to the right person, governed and on time.

### Financial services and insurance

Customer onboarding and KYC checks depend on pulling together identity documents, application forms and risk assessments from several sources before a case can move. [Claims handling](https://www.doxis.com/en/solutions/insurance) has the same shape. An insurer needs the policy, the correspondence and the supporting evidence together in one case file.

[ECM for financial services](https://www.doxis.com/en/solutions/bank-financial-services) gives underwriters and claims teams a [single, searchable customer view](https://www.doxis.com/en/solutions/electronic-files) of each relationship. It also provides the retention and access controls FCA-regulated firms are expected to demonstrate.

### Manufacturing

Engineering drawings, supplier contracts and quality certificates pile up fast across a manufacturing enterprise, each tied to a specific part, project or purchase order. Without a shared platform, that documentation lives wherever the last person who touched it saved it.

[ECM for manufacturing](https://www.doxis.com/en/solutions/manufacturing) links these documents to the ERP process they belong to. A quality audit or a supplier dispute then takes minutes of searching, where it used to take a week of document hunting.

### Energy and utilities

Asset documentation, safety certifications and regulatory filings must stay retrievable for the full life of an asset, which can run for decades. [Energy and utilities firms](https://www.doxis.com/en/solutions/public-utility-companies) use ECM to keep that documentation centralised and audit-proof, connected to the asset management and ERP systems that track the physical infrastructure.

### Transport and logistics

A missing [customs document](https://www.doxis.com/en/solutions/logistics) can hold an entire freight train at the border until a replacement arrives. Kombiverkehr, a European combined road-rail operator that moves more than 800,000 truckloads a year, runs its document processes on Doxis as SaaS for exactly this reason.

- Customs and shipping papers: T1 and shipping documents are available digitally at the terminal and at border crossings, which cuts wait times for customers
- Claims: transport damage claims run through workflows and digital business partner files, giving sales staff a complete view of each customer
- Accounts payable: a new incoming invoice workflow reduced the workload for everyone involved by 30 hours per week

## Replacing a legacy ECM system like Documentum or FileNet

Plenty of UK enterprises are not choosing ECM for the first time. They are [modernising a legacy system](https://www.doxis.com/en/blog/legacy-system) that has been in place for over a decade and no longer gets the vendor investment it once did.

Doxis has documented, production-proven migration support for named legacy platforms, delivered in partnership with HAVI Solutions, SER's dedicated data migration specialist:

- Documentum
- FileNet
- IBM Content Manager
- OpenText

The migration works at the content repository layer, moving content and metadata from the legacy archive into Doxis. That means its complexity depends on the source system and the structure of your data, and the ERP you run has no documented bearing on it.

### Two ways to handle existing content

You can choose per document pool whether content moves now or stays where it is.

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Approach** | **What happens** | **Best for** |
| Leave it in place | Metadata migrates first; content stays in the legacy system and is accessed read-only through a storage adapter | Large volumes you don't need to touch immediately |
| Physically import | Content moves fully into Doxis, fully editable and versionable from day one | Documents your teams need to work with straight away |

Either way, the metadata migration runs through a [defined, four-step migration process](https://www.doxis.com/en/blog/expert-insights/dms-migration-4-steps-to-well-organized-information-management) with a proven toolset, so nobody writes a bespoke script from scratch.

### Map your existing ERP document links early

Many legacy archives rely on [ERP integration](https://www.doxis.com/en/solutions/erp-integration), so that clicking a document button inside a business transaction opens the stored file. SAP ArchiveLink is the best-known example, and other ERP systems use their own linking mechanisms. Those links have to be reconciled as a workstream of their own, alongside the content migration.

Scope them with your ERP team before the migration project starts. Handled early, it is a planned task. Found halfway through, it is a delay.

## Beyond ECM: where content automation is heading

ECM answers where a document lives and who can access it. On its own, it leaves three questions open: what happens to that document next, who needs to act on it, and how the data inside it gets used elsewhere. That is where ECM increasingly connects to two adjacent disciplines: [business process management](https://www.doxis.com/en/business-platform/process-automation), which moves content through decisions, and [intelligent document processing](https://www.doxis.com/en/business-platform/doxis-aidp), which reads the data inside it.

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discipline | What it adds | What it adds |
| ECM | Captures, stores and governs content | Keeps a signed contract findable, versioned and audit-ready |
| Business process management ( [BPM](https://www.doxis.com/en/business-platform/process-automation)) | Routes content through approvals and decisions | Moves an invoice through an exception check before payment |
| Intelligent document processing (IDP) | Uses AI to read and extract data from content | Turns a scanned invoice into structured data a workflow can act on |

Run separately, these three mean three vendor relationships, three sets of integrations and three places where governance can break down. Run as one platform, they become what is increasingly called Intelligent Content Automation: a single system that captures, understands, processes and governs content across its entire lifecycle.

## FAQs for enterprise content management (ECM)

### What does ECM stand for?

ECM stands for enterprise content management. It describes enterprise-wide software that manages business documents and content across their whole lifecycle, in a governed, audit-ready way.

### What is the difference between ECM and a document management system?

A document management system (DMS) stores, versions and retrieves documents. ECM covers the whole content lifecycle across the enterprise, adding retention, records management, process automation and integration with your business applications.

### Is ECM the same as content services?

Content services is the newer term for the same discipline, with more emphasis on delivering content into other applications through connectors and APIs. Most modern ECM platforms, Doxis included, are built as content services platforms.

### How does ECM support UK GDPR and FCA compliance?

ECM applies retention policies, access controls and audit logging automatically, so a firm can demonstrate who accessed a document, when, and prove it was retained or deleted according to the correct policy without a manual review.

### Can ECM integrate with your existing ERP and CRM systems?

Yes. Doxis offers standard CRM integration and Microsoft 365 connectors and a configurable connection layer for ERP systems, so documents stay linked to the business records they support.

### Can ECM run in the cloud?

Yes. Doxis runs on premises, in the cloud or in a hybrid setup, so you can choose the deployment model that fits your security and data residency requirements.

### What is Intelligent Content Automation?

Intelligent Content Automation combines ECM, business process management and AI-powered document processing in one platform. One system handles a document from the moment it arrives until it is deleted.
